answer: Add/Drop Groups are identified by adg-number, an integer in the range [1..110], so a node can have up to 110 ADGs. Use 'add adg-<adg-number>' to create one, 'set adg-<adg-number> label <value>' to label it (String 0..256), and 'delete adg-<adg-number>' to remove it. Whether the same wavelength may appear twice is reported by the read-only (show) attribute wavelength-duplication: 'one-per-adg' (the default) means no duplication of frequencies in the ADG, and 'one-per-degree' means duplication of frequencies is allowed in the ADG but only one at the Degree. Only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other show attributes are max-add-drop-ports (max ports for the ADG) and bands-supported, default standardC-band. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'set amplifier-<name>', gain-target sets the constant-gain value over 0..40 dB, default 0.0, and applies only in manual control-mode. control-mode is auto-max-pw (default, the auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual; amp-control-support shows whether auto-max-pw is permitted ('auto') or 'manual-only'. In auto mode you instead use gain-adjustment, a user offset in [-20.00..20.00] dB, default 0, supported only on amplifiers with function 'pa' or 'inline'. gain-operating reports the actually configured gain (0.0 when the card is out or the EDFA disabled). Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode: 'auto' (default) has the system implicitly control tilt per configured fiber parameters, 'auto-planned' per planning tool parameters, and 'manual' lets the user control it. tilt-target ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) applies in manual mode and raises a warning that the attribute may be traffic affecting; tilt-adjustment ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) offsets the target when mode is auto or auto-planned. When amplifier function is 'add' or 'drop', the only tilt option is 'manual'.

Use 'set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>'. The permitted range is [0, 5..30dB] with a default of 0dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different than auto; if control-mode is 'auto' the parameter is ignored. control-mode values are auto (default; you configure only the span attributes and optionally the pointloss, gain is automatically controlled), auto-planned (you configure the target Raman gain plus span attributes), and manual (basic manual configuration, where even the target pump powers must be configured). To see how many pumps the card has, use 'show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps'; the values are 4 or 2, and this value dictates the number of pump-power objects exposed by the system. Related read-outs are total-pump-power ([-99..99 dBm], -99 means no power), actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain (both 0 when the Raman amplifier or card is disabled).

Switch it on with 'set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled', for example 'set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled'. The default is disabled; enabled means ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum is enabled. The entity can also be created with the value in place: 'add ase-idler-service-<name> [alarm-report-control <value>] [ase-idler-enable <value>]', and removed with 'delete ase-idler-service-<name>'. To see whether it actually came up, read the ase-idler-state attribute with 'show ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-state': ase-enabled (filling complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling incomplete), ase-faulted (signal faulted), or ase-disabled (default, signal completely removed from the band spectrum). oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled) and avail-state are also available; function is 'idler'.

target-output-power is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured, with a range of (-3.00..20.50) dBm and a default of 13. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable (enabled/disabled) defaults to disabled, and the read-only pump-state, which reports the state of the ASE Idler pump, also defaults to disabled. Both are set with 'set ase-idler-source-<name>', for example 'set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00''. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (String 0..256) and alarm-report-control (allowed by default, or inhibited). function is fixed at ase-idler-source. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use the 'calibrate' command, whose syntax is 'calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>'. type has the single value 'raman', which triggers calibration on Raman cards. trigger is 'start' to start the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span, or 'stop' to stop it. entity selects the entity to be calibrated as an instance-identifier; for Raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity. So to kick one off: 'calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line', and to stop it: 'calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line'. None of the three parameters has a default. The command is available in Operational Mode only.

A degree is identified by degree-number, an integer in the range [1..20], and the number must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, so a node can have up to 20 degrees. Manage them with 'add degree-<degree-number>', 'set degree-<degree-number> label <value>', 'delete degree-<degree-number>' and 'show degree-<degree-number>'. For spectral granularity, the show attributes are slot-width-granularity, the width of a slot given in MHz, default 6250, and center-freq-granularity, the granularity of allowed center frequencies in MHz, default 3125, computed from a base frequency of 193.1 THz (G.694.1). Slots are joined to form a media channel between min-slots (default 8) and max-slots (default 32), where min-slots must be less than or equal to max-slots. bands-supported defaults to standardC-band.

On a multi-rail ILA node, direction n and direction n+1 are automatically assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. That is why they come in pairs: the DWDM Line1 port is always assigned an odd index value and the DWDM Line2 port is always assigned an even index value. The direction index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets direction-number from the configured direction-port: 1 when the port is dwdm-line1 and 2 when it is dwdm-line2, and it fills direction-card (card-<chassis>-<slot>) autonomously. The same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. Syntax: 'add direction-<index> direction-port <value> [label <value>]', with 'delete [-f] direction-<index>' forcing without confirmation.

On a dsc facility you can configure only three attributes, using 'add dsc-<name>' or 'set dsc-<name>': label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock or maintenance, default unlock), and alarm-report-control (allowed, the default, or inhibited). Everything else is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. The managed-by attribute describes whether the facility was system created or not; its values are 'system' and 'user' with a default of 'system'. It matters because only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so a dsc reporting managed-by 'system' cannot be removed with 'delete dsc-<name>'. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'add dsc-group-<name>' or 'set dsc-group-<name>' there are two Q signal-degrade thresholds with matching hysteresis. Pre-FEC: pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm, decimal64 with fraction-digits 3, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 implies threshold crossing alarming is disabled and the specific sub-range is per carrier use-case; pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is decimal64 fraction-digits 1, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. Post-FEC: post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, decimal64 fraction-digits 1, range (12.5..18.0) dB, default 18; post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is range (0.1..1.0) dB, default 0.5. Alongside these, dgd-high-threshold raises the DGD-OORH alarm, uint16 range (25..400) ps, default 100.

Use the 'gadt' command, which retrieves golden carrier application information: 'show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>]'. Each of the four parameters, application-description-H, application-description-P, application-description-S and application-description-U, is a string giving the detailed description of that application ID, and none has a default. For example, 'show gadt application-description-H' returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. Running 'show gadt' without a parameter lists them all. The command is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

The 'gapt' command lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT). It is scoped per card type: the syntax is 'show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type]', where card-type is a card type name string, version is the table version (string, length 0..5), and applicable-resource-type is the managed resource type(s) applicable for that particular advanced parameter. Plain 'show gapt' lists the tables and their versions, for example gapt-CHM6 version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 version 3.0, and gapt-CHM7T. Scoping to one card, 'show gapt-chm7', lists that card's parameters as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/<name> entries such as BOASetting, CRAvgNCtrl, ClockPreEmphasis, EEPNNLMitigation, NLC, PDLMitigation, RxCDMode, RxRollOff and TxSignalBWControl, followed by the table version. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the 'gcmt' command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode. The syntax is 'show gcmt [<card-type>] [version]', where the object parameter is the golden carrier modes string and version is the table version. To look up one specific mode, name it directly: 'show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P'. The output lists the resolved mode with its per-card qualification and the mode's characteristics, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with capacity 800 Gbps, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate 95.2965203 GBaud, application P, compatibility-id 6, and status supported. The command is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read the status attribute with 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status'. status describes the carrier mode release status and its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, so a mode reading 'supported' is fully supported while 'experimental' is not. Two related attributes qualify this per subtype: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports (string length 0..32, maximum 20 elements), and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (string length 0..16, maximum 10 elements). The carrier-mode key is a string of 1..15 characters in the format <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, for example 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P. Other readable attributes include actual-carrier-mode, capacity (Gbps), client-mode (ethernet, ethernet-otn), baud-rate, application, compatibility-id and sop-tracking-mode.

The 'l0-capabilities' command shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The syntax is simply 'show l0-capabilities'; the command takes no parameters at all. It is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the OADM-specific limits, the separate 'oadm-capabilities' command reports max-degrees and max-adgs.

To carve out a Media Channel you must supply three mandatory arguments: 'add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value>', optionally followed by [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [auto-delete <value>]. lower-frequency and upper-frequency are the lower and upper frequencies of the Media Channel, given in MHz. parent-oms is an instance-identifier that is only set upon MC creation, and the referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, it cannot be in an ADG. The system then derives center-frequency (in MHz) and slot-width, calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. auto-delete defaults to disabled; when enabled the system auto-deletes the MC once its associated NMC is deleted, and it may only be enabled on RD66TM sleds (l0-mode-op=hsc-ols), always being disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte. Example: 'add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000''.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The 'mc-f' command is used only to show the Media Channel Filler facility attributes, and the sole syntax is 'show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]'. There is no add, set or delete form. Every parameter is listed as used in 'show' only: name (String 0..64), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to the parent and children facilities), supporting-card, supporting-port, AID (String 1..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width, which the system calculates from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency in MHz units. None of these has a default. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Up to four cards per ADG: in 'add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]', the index is a number in the range [1..4], and adg-number is in the range [1..110]. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the card instance identifier. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring has values true and false with a default of true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned; it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. Example: 'add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6'. Access requires Network Administrator or Network Engineer privilege, in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use the 'modules-degree' command: 'add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>'. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. index has the single permitted value 1, since the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the instance identifier of the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. You can later change it with 'set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>', inspect it with 'show modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card', and remove the association with 'delete modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index>'. Example: 'add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1'. Requires Network Administrator or Network Engineer privilege, in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use 'show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power'. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier (channel) in MHz as a uint32. monitored-optical-power is the measured power for that carrier in dBm, decimal64 with range (-99.00..99.00) and default -99, where the value -99.00 means no power. The companion attribute monitored-width (uint32, default 0) gives the carrier width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source/destination, in MHz. Example: 'show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power', or omit the attribute to see all attributes of that channel. The command is show-only, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

center-frequency is the nominal center frequency of the NMC and takes values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. It is mandatory on creation: 'add nmc-<name> parent-facility <value> center-frequency <value>'. width is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000. The user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate (GBd) configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are used in add and show only, so they are fixed at creation and not changeable with 'set'. parent-facility can be either a Media Channel or an OMS, is only set upon creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, not an ADG. Example: 'add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1'.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies an allocated bandwidth of 75000 MHz by default: alloc-bandwidth is a value in MHz units with a default of 75000, bounded by alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency. What is currently in use is reported separately by actual-bandwidth, in MHz units with a default of 0, together with actual-lower-frequency and actual-upper-frequency. It is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, and because this is a system created attribute it is enabled by default, values enabled and disabled. Power read-outs are power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx, both [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99, plus output-attenuation-compensation-actual (decimal64, fraction-digits 2, range -20..20, default 0). Only admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable via 'set nmc-f-<name>'.

Use 'show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]'. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees, reported as 20 (uint8), and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups, reported as 110 (uint8); either is 0 if not supported. Degrees and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for the ILA node-type is 0 by convention because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. Sample output: 'show oadm-capabilities' returns max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110. The command is show-only, in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'set oc-<name>' the loopback attribute takes facility, terminal or none, with a default of none, and is useful to debug on the fiber connection; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal and takes facility or terminal. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern that is injected and takes none (the default), enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 or PRBS31. test-signal-direction takes the single value ingress, which is also the default. test-signal-monitoring monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics and takes true or false, defaulting to false. Example: 'set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false'. All of these are readable back with 'show oc-<name>'. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information. Consequently, when either the OMS monitoring-mode is 'not-monitored' as configured by the user, or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Inspect it with 'show ochm' or 'show ochm-<name>'. The direction attribute is ingress or egress, but currently only egress is supported and it is the default. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, where -99dBm means either that the power is not yet measured, measurement being performed by the OCM at the DGE2 card, or that no power was detected or there is no appropriate fiber-connection; for the egress direction the power actual should be calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, at the same reference point where the target power is defined. target-actual-power (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99) and attenuation-actual (0..55 dB, the DGE VOA attenuation of the channel) apply to HSC OLS nodes. Only label, admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable.
